newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil tax receipts total 95.096 bln reais in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Brazil tax receipts total 95.096 bln reais in 1996.

text.p: Brazil's federal tax receipts totaled 95.096 billion reais in 1996 versus 84 billion reais in 1995, the Internal Revenue Service said.
The service said in a statement that when adjusted for inflation, 1996 tax receipts were 97.53 billion reais versus 95.74 the previous year, a 1.87 percent increase.
The statement said that tax receipts in December were 10.304 billion reais, a 24.34 percent increase in real inflation-adjusted terms over December 1995's 8.287 billion reais.
"Revenue in 1996 represented a historical record for the Internal Revenue Service," the statement said.

It said the tax receipts gradually improved in the second half of 1996, showing a real 6.78 percent increase over the same 1995 period, and reversing a 2.78 percent drop in year-on-year receipts in the first half.
It said the main reasons for the better 1996 results were:
* Payments by financial institutions that lost court challenges on their taxes.
* Changes in corporate tax laws which resulted in a real increase of 24.14 percent in corporate tax receipts from 1995 to 1996.
* A surge in vehicle sales resulting in a 47.26 percent rise in auto taxes.
* A crackdown on overdue taxes and increasing revenue from fines, which rose 15.35 percent over 1995.
On the downside, revenues were hurt by a reduction in the number of taxable imports, mainly cars, and a lowering of taxes on credit operations.
"With the positive factors outweighing the negative, the final result exceeded the target set by the Internal Revenue Service," it said.
